questions.subject: Unit 2 • World Geography (Local Winds and Wind Systems)
questions.question:
Match List I (local winds) with List II (the region or country where each occurs).

List I
A. Chinook
B. Föhn
C. Harmattan
D. Brickfielder

List II
1. From the Sahara towards the Gulf of Guinea in West Africa
2. Eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains in North America
3. Northern slopes of the Alps in Switzerland
4. Victoria, Australia

Choose the correct code:
questions.verificationSource: G. C. Leong, Certificate Physical and Human Geography
questions.explanation: The Chinook is a warm, dry downslope wind on the eastern side of the Rocky Mountains and is sometimes called a 'snow-eater' because it can rapidly melt snow (A–2). The Föhn is a warm downslope wind associated with the Alps (B–3). The Harmattan is a dry wind blowing from the Sahara towards the Gulf of Guinea and is sometimes nicknamed the 'doctor wind' (C–1). The Brickfielder is a hot, dry wind associated with southeastern Australia, including Victoria (D–4).

questions.subject: Unit 2 • World Geography (Ocean Currents)
questions.question: Which of the following ocean currents is NOT a cold current?
questions.explanation: The Agulhas Current is a warm current flowing southward along the southeast coast of Africa in the southwest Indian Ocean. In contrast, the Canary Current off northwestern Africa, the Benguela Current off southwestern Africa, and the Humboldt (Peru) Current off the western coast of South America are generally classified as cold currents.

questions.subject: Unit 2 • World Geography (Latitude, Longitude and Time Calculation)
questions.question: If the local time at Greenwich (0° longitude) is 10:00 a.m., what are the local times at a town on 60° E longitude and another town on 45° W longitude, respectively?
questions.verificationSource: NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography
questions.explanation: Earth rotates 360° in approximately 24 hours, so local time changes by about four minutes per degree of longitude. A location 60° east of Greenwich is 240 minutes (four hours) ahead: 10:00 a.m. + 4 hours = 2:00 p.m. A location 45° west is 180 minutes (three hours) behind: 10:00 a.m. − 3 hours = 7:00 a.m. The correct pair is 2:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.
